transcript: Sunday, decided I'm actually going to fix this sleep situation instead of just complaining about it in these entries every week. Looked up blackout curtains online, ordering a set tomorrow. Small concrete step but it feels better than just enduring another month of four a.m. wake-ups.

Blackout curtains arrived and got them hung tonight, whole apartment's a different place in the dark now, no more streetlight glow leaking in at all hours. It's such a small thing, curtains, but after months of bad sleep tangled up with Atlas and then with grief, doing something concrete and physical about it felt genuinely hopeful in a way I haven't felt in a while. Going to test them out tonight and see if it actually makes a difference. Fingers crossed this is the fix.

First full night behind the new curtains and I actually slept, properly slept, no four a.m. wide-eyed staring at the ceiling. Woke up with the alarm instead of before it for the first time in what feels like forever. Small thing, curtains, but the difference this morning is not small at all.

Atlas still heavy, still grinding, but I'm facing it on actual sleep now which makes a bigger difference than I expected. Same amount of work feels less impossible when you're not running on fumes. Long day regardless, but a manageable one.

Pottery Thursday, decent session, working on trimming technique now that the basic forms are getting more consistent. The instructor's pushing me a little harder each week which I appreciate even when it's frustrating in the moment.

Easy evening with Sam, nothing planned, just ended up cooking a simple dinner together and talking for hours about nothing in particular. These low-key nights keep being the best part of most weeks. Grateful for the steadiness of it.

Longer run this Saturday, pushing distance again now that sleep's stabilized and legs have some energy back. Felt strong most of the way, that good kind of tired at the end instead of depleted. Thinking about signing up for something bigger later in the spring, a half marathon maybe, we'll see.

My brother called today. Dario. We hadn't talked, actually talked, in two years, not since everything fell apart after Dad left and we both said things we probably shouldn't have and then just let the silence do the rest of the damage on its own. I saw his name come up on my phone and just stared at it ringing for what felt like a full minute before I picked up. His voice sounded the same, which was strange, like no time had passed at all even though so much has. He said he'd heard about Nonna from Mom, that he was sorry he wasn't at the funeral, and I could hear in how he said it that it cost him something to make this call at all. We didn't get into the actual fight, what caused the distance in the first place, that felt too big for a first call, but we talked for almost an hour about smaller things, work, his apartment, whether I was still running. It's strange, hopeful and cautious at the same time, like standing at the edge of something you're not sure is solid yet. I don't know where this goes from here. But I'm glad he called.

Overcast this Monday, one of the fewer ones this month, spring apparently starting to push the gray away a little. Still turning yesterday's call with Dario over in my head at odd moments during the day, couldn't quite focus fully on work. Not in a bad way, just present, taking up space.

Still thinking about the call with Dario honestly, replaying pieces of it, wondering if I should text him something or just wait for him to reach out again. Decided to wait, don't want to seem overeager and scare off whatever this fragile new thing is. Work otherwise unremarkable today.

Frustrating day at work, Atlas hit another blocker that's apparently going to push the timeline out yet again, which after months of this feels less surprising than it probably should. Vented about it a little to Sam over dinner, mostly just needed to say it out loud to someone.

Pottery Thursday, needed it after this week's frustrations at work. Something calming about the repetitive motion of centering clay, forces you to just be present with your hands instead of your head. Made a small planter, first non-vessel thing I've tried.
Friday, tired, small quiet plans for the weekend. Nothing much to report today, just glad the week's over. Atlas timeline slip still bothering me a little in the background.

Sharp pain in my knee about three miles into today's run, had to stop and walk the rest of the way home limping a little. Scared me honestly, more than the pain itself, this immediate fear of losing running right when it's become the thing that keeps me steady through everything else this year, the burnout, the grief, all of it. Iced it when I got home, going to book a physio appointment this week instead of just hoping it goes away on its own like I usually do with these things. Trying not to catastrophize but it's hard not to.

Forced rest day, knee still tender, restless about it all day, kept eyeing my running shoes by the door like they were mocking me. Booked the physio appointment for next week at least, that's something. Hard to sit still when moving is usually how I process everything.

Monday but the sun actually broke through this morning, first real sunshine in what feels like weeks, whole commute felt different because of it. Knee still bothering me a little but not as sharp as Saturday. Small mood lift just from the light.

First physio appointment today, turns out it's something with the patellar tendon, overuse pattern from ramping distance up too fast without enough recovery built in, classic beginner mistake apparently. Gave me a set of exercises to do, nothing dramatic, should heal fine with some patience and actually following the plan instead of just pushing through pain like I usually do. Relief honestly, better than the vague dread I'd been carrying since Saturday.

Bad Atlas day, something in the underlying architecture snapping in a way that's going to cost us another week at least, and I could feel something in me snapping a little too when Priya delivered the news in standup. Didn't say anything I regret, but it was close. Tired of this project in a way I haven't let myself fully admit until today.

Pottery tonight, wedging clay and genuinely thinking, seriously thinking, about what it would look like to just quit the job. Not in a dramatic way, just turning the actual math over in my head, savings, timeline, what I'd even do instead. Didn't say any of that out loud to anyone in the class obviously, just let the thought sit there while my hands worked. Strange how the quietest activities let the loudest thoughts in.

Actually opened the notes app tonight and drafted a resignation letter. Just to see how it felt to put words to it. It felt terrifying and also strangely clarifying, seeing the sentences laid out, I am writing to inform you of my decision to resign, all the formal language sitting there waiting for a name and a date. Didn't send it obviously, don't even know if I'm actually going to. What stopped me wasn't fear exactly, more just not wanting to make a huge decision from inside a bad week instead of from someplace steadier. Going to sit with the draft for now, saved but not sent, and see how I feel once Atlas actually ships and some of this pressure lifts.

Talked through the whole resignation-draft thing with Sam tonight, first time I'd said any of it out loud to another person. They didn't tell me what to do, just asked good questions, whether it was really the job or just this project, whether I'd talked to Priya directly about how bad it's gotten. Good questions honestly, ones I didn't have great answers for yet. Feels lighter having said it out loud at least.

Grief wave today, out of nowhere again the way it does. Was making a simple Sunday sauce, nothing fancy, and the smell of it simmering just pulled Nonna right into the room with me, so vividly it almost hurt, her recipe card in my head even though I don't actually have the physical card, just the memory of watching her write it years ago in her looping handwriting. Cried a little over the pot, which felt okay actually, felt like the right response rather than something to push down. Six weeks now and it still finds me in the smallest moments.

Monday, steadier today than yesterday's wave, gray but not overcast exactly, just quiet weather. Work manageable. Doing the physio exercises before bed most nights now, actually sticking with a routine for once.

Lunch with Maya, finally said the quitting thing out loud to her too, the resignation draft and everything. She wasn't shocked, said she'd sensed something building for months honestly, which was both a little alarming and a little validating. Good to have it out in the open with someone who knows me this well.
Midweek, mundane, Atlas grinding on but no new fires today at least. Small mercy. Physio exercises done, knee feeling noticeably better this week.

Pottery Thursday, good session, glazed a few pieces from a couple weeks ago, curious to see how the colors turn out once they're fired. This class keeps being the steadiest, most reliable good hour of every week regardless of what else is going on.

Physio follow-up today, knee's healing well apparently, ahead of the usual timeline they said, probably because I actually did the exercises this time instead of just nodding along and ignoring them. Exercises themselves are boring, I won't pretend otherwise, a lot of slow controlled leg lifts that don't feel like much, but clearly they're working. Cleared for gradually building distance back up next week.

Short careful run this morning, first one since the knee scare, kept the pace easy and the distance short on purpose. Held up fine, no sharp pain, just a little awareness of it that's probably normal after weeks off. Cautiously relieved. Spring air out there too, first real hint of warmth in a while.

Texted Dario back tonight, small step, just asked how his week went. He responded quick, seemed genuinely happy to hear from me. Nothing deep yet, but it's something, a thread staying open instead of going quiet again.

Month's closing out, and spring is genuinely starting to show itself, the light lingering later, a little warmth in the afternoons. Been a strange month, the curtains actually fixing my sleep, Dario calling after two years of silence, the knee scare, the resignation draft still sitting unsent in my notes app. A lot of threads still open heading into April. Trying to just let them unfold instead of forcing any of them.
